subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add a distinct soft-steer lifecycle that aborts or pauses an active run, preserves the required state, injects user guidance, and resumes the task rather than retaining the current boundary-steer plus explicit-interrupt model?
rationale: The existing modes deliberately separate boundary delivery from abort-and-replace behavior; choosing transparent continuation semantics determines user-visible guarantees, backend requirements, and session-state safety.

options.title: Sponsor a scoped soft-steer contract
options.body: Define supported runner phases, treatment of in-flight tools and partial output, and transcript/queue guarantees before implementing one canonical lifecycle.

options.title: Retain the current two-mode model
options.body: Keep boundary steering and explicit interrupt as separate behaviors, documenting that immediate continuation is not guaranteed.

options.title: Narrow to a boundary-steering regression
options.body: Limit work to cases where current steer should reach an active runner at safe boundaries and track transparent resume as a separate future proposal.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a scoped soft-steer contract
recommendation.body: Define supported runner phases, treatment of in-flight tools and partial output, and transcript/queue guarantees before implementing one canonical lifecycle.
